paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Peter is not saying "watch out for scary people out there." He says there will be false teachers "among you," and they will "secretly introduce destructive heresies" (2 Peter 2:1). They don't show up wearing a sign. They show up with "lofty but empty words" (2 Peter 2:18), and a fancy box with a bow and NOTHING inside.

So how do you spot them? Peter says to look at what they promise and what they are. They promise freedom, but they are slaves themselves, because "a man is a slave to whatever has mastered him" (2 Peter 2:19). Their pitch is smooth, but their greed and their hunger for sin give them away (2 Peter 2:3, 14). The way to catch a fake is to know the real thing, and that means knowing the Word of God.

And here's the good news, baker. Peter lines up Noah and Lot to show that "the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trials" (2 Peter 2:9). Lot lived in the middle of all that mess, and God still knew right where he was. But Peter also warns that turning back after knowing "the way of righteousness" is worse than never knowing it (2 Peter 2:21). So stay close to Jesus, keep your ovens ready, and don't go back to the mud.
